question.text: 'Mahanadi PE Fund II' (Cat II AIF) holds 18% in 'Konark Tech Ltd' pre-IPO. Konark Tech is now filing its DRHP. Under SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018, what is the lock-in applicable to the Cat II AIF's pre-issue shareholding post-IPO allotment?

answer.text: 3 years, as the AIF is deemed part of the promoter group
No lock-in: AIFs are exempt from ICDR lock-in
6 months from date of allotment in the public issue, extended to 1 year if the majority of the IPO fresh-issue proceeds are deployed for capital expenditure
18 months uniformly, similar to promoter contribution

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, the entire pre-issue share capital of an issuer, other than the minimum promoter contribution, is locked in for 6 months from the date of allotment in the public issue. This period extends to 1 year where the majority of the fresh-issue proceeds are intended for capital expenditure. A Cat II/III AIF holding pre-issue shares is subject to this lock-in alongside other pre-issue shareholders. The Trap: Option A treats an 18% AIF holding as promoter group, which is not how the ICDR lock-in operates. Option B overstates the position by claiming a blanket exemption from ICDR lock-in for AIFs. Option D applies an 18-month uniform lock-in that does not match the ICDR pre-issue lock-in rule. Note: The structural rule is 6 months for pre-issue capital other than minimum promoter contribution, stretched to 1 year if the IPO fresh-issue proceeds are predominantly for capex; the AIF's holding sits within this rule, not within a promoter lock-in.
